# MLAI marketing/docs — design and scope record

The user approved moving from the supplied audit into implementation. Repository reads corrected its greenfield premise: an active MLAI website already exists. This build stays in an isolated review directory and does not modify that application.

## Design

An editorial engineering site: white canvas, near-black typography, restrained green actions, a dark conceptual architecture panel, distinct project accents, open project rows, and a legible documentation shell. No generated hero image or external font is required. No approved image reference existed, so no screenshot-fidelity claim is made.

## Functional scope

Eighteen pages plus 404: home, directory, four project pages, nine docs pages, trust, about, and a local project-brief composer. Working local docs search; project filters encoded in URL state; conceptual layer selection; code/article copying with explicit fallback; brief generation, copy, and text download; responsive menus; keyboard dialogs; dark mode; reduced motion. No remote backend, accounts, lead submission, model calls, analytics, or production integration.

## Content model

One typed collection defines source references, projects, article sections, and evidence labels. It drives TSX rendering, generated MDX, navigation, and search. Source review and reported test coverage are distinct from independently measured behavior. No numbers are used as fabricated performance evidence.

## Verification boundaries

The offline exporter uses a review-only JSX serializer. Its output is a functional review, not a Next build. The Next source uses Fumadocs Core/MDX headlessly, custom UI, and a small client enhancement lifecycle. Native controls avoid unverified primitive-library dependencies. The real framework build and integration into the current `apps/web` remain separate gates.
